name: Gana
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2013. The Austronesian languages. Revised edition. Asia-Pacific Linguistics Open Access Monographs 8. Canberra: ANU. ch. 4 (languages of Borneo).
sources.note: Areal remark only, Gana not named: 'Unlike the Philippines, stress is not phonemic in any language of Borneo. However, unlike much of the AN world, where stress falls predictably on the penult, many of the languages of coastal Sarawak, and some interior languages have final stress in citation forms, but penultimate stress in phrasal context.'

sources.citation: Combrink, Hans J. B., Craig Soderberg, Michael E. Boutin & Alanna Y. Boutin (comps.) 2008. Indigenous groups of Sabah: an annotated bibliography of linguistic and anthropological sources. Rev. ed. SIL e-Books 7. Dallas: SIL. Part 1 (Authors) s.v. Deal, Ribus Tingadon, Tingadon; Part 2 (Ethnic group index) s.v. GANA.
sources.note: Bibliographic only: identifies the unpublished primary descriptions -- Deal 1986 'Gana phonology' (6 pp. MS, 'A phonological description of the Gana sound system', SIL), Deal 1986 'Grammar sketch of Kuijau and Gana' (13 pp.), Ribus Tingadon 1985 'Bahasa Murut dialek Gana' (96 pp. MS, 'chapters on Gana Murut morphology and phonology', Malay, SIL library).

sources.citation: Mahali, Saidatul Nornis Hj. 2024. Ragam-ragam bahasa Murut di Sabah. Jurnal Melayu 23(1). doi:10.17576/jmelayu.2024.2301.03
sources.note: Gana named only in lists of Murut subgroups; no Gana data.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. (sec. 11.4.2 Gana p.395; Gana pronouns pp.143-144; Gana rows in SWSABAH comparative tables)
sources.note: Nothing on Gana or Murutic stress; Gana forms carry no accent marks. Only stress remarks concern Philippine languages (8.2.9; fn.3 p.287 'most languages native to Mindanao and areas further south have lost contrastive stress').

sources.citation: Kroeger, Paul R. 1994 [rev. 2013]. Vowel harmony, neutralization and inalterability in Dusun vs. Murut. Paper presented at 7-ICAL, Leiden.
sources.note: Kimaragang (penultimate or final, not fully predictable) and Timugon ('consistently penultimate', citing Prentice 1971) only; nothing on Gana.

sources.citation: Spitzack, John A. 1984. The Murutic language family. In Julie K. King & John Wayne King (eds.), Languages of Sabah: a survey report, 155-223. Pacific Linguistics C-78. Canberra: ANU. (sec. 4.1 Gana language, pp.190-192; whole volume checked)
sources.note: Nothing; lexicostatistics, intelligibility testing, ethnonyms (Gana/Ganaq/Minansut). The word 'stress' does not occur anywhere in the volume (a full-text search for stress/accent count 0).
sources.venue: Languages of Sabah: a survey report

sources.citation: Prentice, D. J. 1971. The Murut languages of Sabah. Pacific Linguistics C-18. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Timugon stress penultimate (sec. 2.2.1 p.14); ch.10 outline studies cover Timugon subdialects, Nabay, Baukan, Paluan, Sumambuq, Alumbis, Okolod only -- no Minansut/Gana section, so no Gana statement.

sources.citation: Prentice, D. J. 1970. The linguistic situation in northern Borneo. In S. A. Wurm & D. C. Laycock (eds.), Pacific linguistic studies in honour of Arthur Capell, 369-408. Pacific Linguistics C-13. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. 'Minansut' (= Gana) appears only in the nomenclature matrix (p.371), an informant anecdote (pp.371-372: '/j/ occurred mostly in foreign words') and the lexicostatistical table; classification survey, no prosody.
sources.venue: Pacific linguistic studies in honour of Arthur Capell
